entries.why: the swing setter (obj, value, flag): strb [obj+0x28]; the first 8 words equal, and the page SWING of the Pattern menu calls it in the emulator
the length setter: strb [obj+0x29], then the bar copy; the first 8 words equal, called by the page LENGTH in the emulator
the beat setter: strb [obj+0x2a]; the Sampler's also tells the sound engine (parameter 0x3B), the synth's does not; both called by the page BEAT in the emulator
the chord set setter: strb [obj+0x2d]; the first 8 words equal, called by the page CHORD SET in the emulator
the pattern level setter: strb [obj+0x2e] and the sound engine copy; the first 8 words equal, called by the page PATTERN LEVEL in the emulator
the gate arp setter: strb [obj+0x35]; the first 8 words equal, called by the page GATE ARP in the emulator
the alternate setter (obj, which, value, flag): strb [obj+0x48+which]; the first 8 words equal, called by the pages ALTERNATE 13-14 and 15-16 in the emulator
the chain to setter: strh [obj+0x3b04]; the first 8 words equal, called by the page CHAIN TO in the emulator
the chain repeat setter: strb [obj+0x3b06]; the first 8 words equal, called by the page CHAIN REPEAT in the emulator
the tempo getter: ldrh r0, [r0, #0x26]; bx lr, in the same row of getters in both
the bar copy the length setter ends in; the first 8 words equal
the observer report every pattern setter ends with (value change to the windows); the first 8 words equal
the sound engine copy writer (obj+0x401C, parameter, value) the level and alternate setters call; read side by side

the part setter (window, 0x10 + part or 0, part, parameter number, value and 0 on the stack): the knob handler of LEVEL, the SAMPLE and the IFX encoder call it in both; the synth's has no busy check and dispatches through its own table
the window object the part setter gets in r0: the literal at the synth's LEVEL knob call
the last step setter (parts, part, value, flag): strb [obj+0x330*part+0x804]; 12 words equal
the mute setter of a part: clamp 1, strb +0x805, sound engine parameter 0x12; 12 words equal
the voice assign setter: clamp 3, strb +0x806, parameter 0x13; 12 words equal
the motion sequence setter: strb +0x807, parameter 0x14; 12 words equal
the pad velocity setter: strb +0x808, parameter 0x15; 12 words equal
the scale mode setter: strb +0x809; 12 words equal
the part priority setter: strb +0x80a, parameter 0x17; 12 words equal
the amp EG setter: strb +0x81e, parameter 0x28; 12 words equal
the MFX send setter: strb +0x81f, parameter 0x29; 12 words equal
the groove type setter: strb +0x820; the Sampler's clamps to 0x3d, Korg's to 0x18, the rest is the same code
the groove depth setter: strb +0x821; 10 words equal
the IFX on setter: strb +0x824, parameter 0x2c; 12 words equal
the master effect touch setter (obj+0x4004, value, flag): strb [blk+0x3c], parameter 2; 12 words equal
the master effect pad X setter: strb [blk+0x3e], parameter 4; 12 words equal
the master effect pad Y setter: strb [blk+0x3f], parameter 5; 12 words equal
the master effect hold setter: strb [blk+0x41], parameter 6; 12 words equal
the global setter of triggerMode (globals, value, flag), byte 29 of the block: loads the trigger object, then strb; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of velocityCurve (globals, value, flag), byte 27 of the block: strb only; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)

the global setter of clockMode (globals, value, flag), byte 40 of the block: refused while the transport state is 6 to 9, parameter 0x31; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of channel (globals, value, flag), byte 41 of the block: parameter 0x32; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of receiveFilter (globals, value, flag), byte 43 of the block: parameter 0x39; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of sendFilter (globals, value, flag), byte 42 of the block: parameter 0x38; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of syncPolarity (globals, value, flag), byte 17 of the block: parameter 0x2d; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of syncUnit (globals, value, flag), byte 18 of the block: parameter 0x3a; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of metronome (globals, value, flag), byte 16 of the block: strb only; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of tempoLock (globals, value, flag), byte 36 of the block: parameter 0x37, then the tempo; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of knobMode (globals, value, flag), byte 28 of the block: strb only; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of touchScaleRange (globals, value, flag), byte 38 of the block: parameter 0x35; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of lcdContrast (globals, value, flag), byte 30 of the block: parameter 0x36; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of audioInThru (globals, value, flag), byte 20 of the block: parameter 0x2e; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of batteryMode (globals, value, flag), byte 32 of the block: strb only; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of autoPowerOff (globals, value, flag), byte 33 of the block: parameter 0x34; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of powerSave (globals, value, flag), byte 37 of the block: parameter 0x33; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of patternChangeLock (globals, value, flag), byte 19 of the block: strb only; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the global setter of chainMode (globals, value, flag), byte 31 of the block: strb, then the chain state when 0; the page of the Global menu writes through it in both (emulator)
the key and scale cache the key, scale and scale mode setters fill (same layout from here in both, emulator)
the chord tables the chord set setter touches (bytes inside the 0x30 from here change in both, emulator)
